# Module ai

Typed calls to language models. Ask for a value of any type, and the reply
is checked against that type and decoded into it.

```eye
import ai
```

## Types

### AiError {#AiError}

```eye
pub type AiError =
  | Malformed(reply: String, problems: List(String))
  | Declined(reason: String)
  | ProviderError(status: Int, message: String)
```

Why a model call gave no value.

- <span id="AiError-Malformed"></span>`Malformed(reply: String, problems: List(String))`: The reply didn't match the type asked for, even after asking once more
  with the problems listed.
- <span id="AiError-Declined"></span>`Declined(reason: String)`: The model declined to answer.
- <span id="AiError-ProviderError"></span>`ProviderError(status: Int, message: String)`: The provider answered with an error.

### Provider {#Provider}

```eye
pub type Provider =
  | Anthropic
  | OpenAI
  | Gateway
```

Who answers a model call.

- <span id="Provider-Anthropic"></span>`Anthropic`: Anthropic's Messages API, at `ANTHROPIC_URL` or api.anthropic.com, with
  the key `secret("anthropic-api-key")`.
- <span id="Provider-OpenAI"></span>`OpenAI`: OpenAI's chat completions, at `OPENAI_URL` or api.openai.com, with the
  key `secret("openai-api-key")`.
- <span id="Provider-Gateway"></span>`Gateway`: An OpenAI-compatible server at `AI_URL`, such as a gateway that serves
  many models, with the key `secret("ai-key")` if it needs one.

### Tool {#Tool}

```eye
pub extern type Tool
```

A function a model may call. A function declared with `fn` and named where
a Tool is expected becomes one, as in `tools: [searchIssues, label]`: its
parameters give the input schema, required unless they have a default, and
its `##` comment the description. Its parameters and result need `Schema`.
A Tool can't be saved, so it is made where it is used.

## Functions

### generate {#generate}

```eye
@host("ai.generate")
pub extern fn generate(
  model: String,
  system: String = "",
  prompt: String,
  provider: Option(Provider) = None,
  tools: List(Tool) = [],
  approve: fn(String) -> Decision = fn _: Declined,
) -> Result(a, AiError) uses {net Ai.generate}
```

Asks a model for a value of the type the result is used as: its JSON
Schema comes from that type, and the reply is checked and decoded into it.
In a job, `ai.generate!(…)` is a recorded step, so a resumed run neither
calls the model again nor pays twice.

Without `provider:`, a gateway answers every call when `AI_URL` is set;
otherwise the model's name decides: `claude-…` is [`Anthropic`](./ai#Provider-Anthropic), `gpt-…` and
`o1`, `o3`, `o4` … are [`OpenAI`](./ai#Provider-OpenAI).

A `@budget` on the job or function counts each reply's tokens and price. A
call is sent only if the budget leaves room for its prompt and some reply,
and the reply is cut off where the budget ends; a call that doesn't fit
ends the run as `Failed(OverBudget)`.

`tools:` are functions the model may call, each a [`Tool`](./ai#Tool). The model gets
their names, `##` comments and input schemas; when a reply calls one, the
function runs and its result goes back, until the model answers without
calling one. In a job each reply and each tool's result is a step of its
own. A `@destructive` tool runs only with an `Approval`: for each call the
model makes of it, `approve:` is given the call written out, as
`label(issue: 8, name: "dup")`, and is usually
`fn call: approval!(call, from: someone, within: 1 day)`. Without it every
such call is declined.

A call's effect is `net Ai.generate`, and its tools add theirs, so a public
function that calls it lists them all in its `uses`.
